# Recipe — add a dialog

**Use when:** you need a modal that returns a typed result to its caller. **Never** hand-create the
prefab or copy an existing dialog folder (rule #13).

**Widgets have their own recipe** — [`add-widget.md`](./add-widget.md). A widget carries a
composition decision a dialog does not (authored nested prefab vs runtime-instantiated), and taking
it wrong is what ships an unreviewable layout. Toasts follow the shape below: swap the manifest and
read the table in §3.

## 1. Edit the manifest

`Tools/Codegen/Manifests/Scaffold/game.dialogs.json` — append one entry:

```json
{ "id": "Reward" }
```

That is the whole entry. `Manifests/Scaffold/` is deliberately **excluded from the codegen key
scan** (the top-level `*.json` scan is non-recursive), so these never reach the key emitter.

## 2. Run the scaffold

```
Framework/Scaffold/Sync        (editor menu)
```

## 3. What lands

| Kind | Prefab (a **variant** of the framework template) | Controller | View |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Dialog** | `Assets/<Sku>/Content/UI/Reward/Prefabs/RewardDialog.prefab` | `Features/RewardDialog/Presentation/RewardDialog.cs` | `Views/RewardDialog/RewardDialogView.cs` |
| **Widget** | `…/Prefabs/RewardWidget.prefab` | `Features/RewardWidget/Presentation/RewardWidget.cs` | `Views/…/RewardView.cs` |

The controller lands in the feature's `Presentation/` subfolder (`namespace Game.Presentation`) with
a `Game.Presentation.asmref` beside it; the View stays under `Assets/<Sku>/Views/`, where
`Game.Views`' own asmdef already owns it — a View is addressed by prefab, not by feature.
| ↳ | *only in the **composed** mode — an **authored** widget has no manifest entry and no prefab of its own. Decide first: [`add-widget.md`](./add-widget.md) §1.* | | |
| **Toast** | `…/Prefabs/RewardToast.prefab` | *(none — a toast has no controller)* | `Views/…/RewardView.cs` |

The dialog template's required node is **`SafeArea`, and only that**. The prefab is a **Prefab
Variant** of the package template, so a framework template improvement flows into every SKU dialog.

### Never author a `Backdrop` node in a dialog prefab

The two things behind a dialog are **service-owned** and neither belongs on your prefab:

| | What it is | Cardinality | Asset |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Input gate** | invisible full-rect raycast target | **one per modal dialog** — it must sit directly beneath the dialog it protects | `PF/Blocker` (alpha `0`) |
| **Dim** | the darkened screen | **one per modal *stack*** — raised when the modal stack goes empty → non-empty, destroyed when it returns to empty | `PF/DialogDim` |

Blocking input is a property of *a dialog*; dimming is a property of *the stack*. The gate is now fully
transparent, so a `Backdrop` node on your prefab is the **second** dimming surface, and it composites
with the service's: ArrowJourney's 0.65 node over the service's 0.60 dim read as
1 − 0.40 × 0.35 = **0.86** instead of 0.60. It also does not scale — the service's dim is one per stack,
but a prefab node is one per *dialog*, so it comes back as a depth-dependent dim the moment two dialogs
stack.

**No gate catches a re-added `Backdrop`.** `requiredNodes` is a *presence* contract: `Scaffold.Sync
--check` fails a base template that is **missing** `SafeArea`, and fails a variant that **strips** an
inherited node. There is no forbidden-node concept anywhere, so a `Backdrop` node added back to a
template or a dialog prefab is caught by **review only**. Treat this section as the rule.

**Opacity has exactly one home: the `PF/DialogDim` prefab.** Not C#, not `framework.config.json`.

`DialogOptions(Modeless: true)` opts out of both — no gate, no dim count.

## 4. Write the controller

`RewardDialog` extends `DialogBase<TResult>` — a **plain class, never a `MonoBehaviour`**. It owns
every decision; the View owns none.

**`ShowAsync` returns a reason, not a bare value.** A dead scope is an *expected* outcome, not an
exception: the `Aborted` reason makes "the screen died while the dialog was open" impossible to
ignore at the call site — exactly where a bare `T` would silently grant a reward twice.

```
var result = await _dialogs.ShowAsync<RewardDialog, RewardResult>(args, ct);
if (result.Reason == DialogCloseReason.Aborted) return;   // handle it — do not fall through
```

## 5. Animating the dialog — declared in C#, never on the prefab

A dialog animates by declaring a **transition**. It is a plain object the framework constructs and binds
at runtime, so **no prefab is edited and nothing has to be attached** (AD-ANIM-6). On your
`…DialogView : DialogViewBase`:

```csharp
public override ViewTransition CreateTransition()
    => ViewTransition.Combine(new FadeTransition(0.2f), new ScaleTransition(0.92f));
```

**To give every dialog the same feel, register one default instead** — implement
`IDialogTransitionFactory` and register it in your SKU installer. A dialog that declares nothing inherits
it, so a new dialog needs *zero* animation code; a dialog's own `CreateTransition()` always wins. Return a
**fresh instance** per call: each dialog binds to its own view and holds a live tween handle.

Shipped: `FadeTransition` (a `CanvasGroup` — added at runtime if the prefab has none) and
`ScaleTransition` (the view root). Slide is SKU work; it is safe-rect- and layout-coupled.

**Rules for a custom `ViewTransition`.** `SnapTo(true)` must produce exactly the state `PlayShowAsync`
ends in, and `SnapTo(false)` exactly the state it starts from — the framework calls `SnapTo`, you never
do. Cancelling `ct` must **stop** the visual, not abandon it (`MotionHandle.ToUniTask(ct)` does this for
you). Ensure whatever you need on the GameObject in `Bind` (`GetComponent` else `AddComponent`) — **never
require the prefab to carry something**. A null target or a non-positive duration is an immediate no-op.

**What the framework guarantees, so you don't:** the view is snapped hidden before any frame renders; it
is snapped shown and made interactable after your show leg, **even if you override `OnShowAsync` without
calling `base`**; the dialog is non-interactable for the whole transition; a leg that hangs is cancelled
after a cap (`DialogTransitions.DefaultTimeoutMs`) so it can never deadlock teardown; a leg that throws is
logged and the dialog proceeds; and the show and hide legs can never overlap on one view. On an `Aborted`
force-close both legs are skipped entirely.

The cap bounds a leg **two** ways — it cancels the token you were handed *and* races the await — so even a
leg that never reads its `ct` cannot deadlock teardown. Honour `ct` anyway: only cancelling actually stops
your tween; the race merely stops the framework waiting for it.

**Don't** use `UniTask.Delay` in the controller to time a `void` View animation — that splits one duration
across the human and machine zones. **Don't** opt into `DialogOptions(Modeless: true)` just to animate the
dim; `IDialogTransitionFactory.CreateForBackdrop()` drives it, configured in code beside the dialog
default. That leg belongs to the **stack**: it plays once when the first modal opens and once when the
last one closes, composed with that dialog's hide under a single cap. A mid-stack close animates its
dialog alone — the dim is not leaving.

Widgets and toasts do **not** have this seam driven for them yet — see the spine's Deferred table.

## 6. Layout is human zone

The prefab's **uGUI layout** — the hierarchy, the `TextProxy` TMP text-layer stacks, anchors — is
**human zone** (rule #12). Do it through **Unity-MCP against a live editor**, never by editing the
`.prefab` YAML. Raw YAML edits corrupt GUIDs and fileIDs.

That is a rule about **mechanism, not authority**: it fixes *how* you edit the prefab, not *who
decides what it looks like*. Absent an artist spec, the aesthetic call is yours — rule #17 and
the `pf-visual-design` skill.

## 7. Gate

```
Framework/Scaffold/Check       # the prefab-variant + class legs
```

Plus both View tests at review (`AGENTS.framework.md` §3).

**Visual finish (rule #17).** The dialog ships finished, not greyboxed: walk the eight-point checklist
in the `pf-visual-design` skill and take a capture at FHD in the SKU's own orientation (1080x1920
portrait, 1920x1080 landscape — never the tool's default). Colours and spacing come from the SKU's
`DesignTokens`.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| The dialog opens but the result is always default | The `Aborted` reason is being ignored at the call site. |
| The View has an `if (canAfford)` branch | Violates the "why" test — move the decision to the controller and expose `SetBuyEnabled(bool)`. |
| The prefab lost its template link | It was hand-created instead of scaffolded, so it is not a Prefab Variant. Delete it and re-run `Scaffold.Sync`. |
| A `.prefab` diff is enormous and full of fileID churn | Someone edited YAML directly. Revert and redo through Unity-MCP. |
| The screen gets darker with every dialog you stack | Something is dimming per dialog. Find the `Backdrop` node on the prefab or template and delete it — the dim is service-owned, one per stack. No gate reports this; it is a review catch. |
| The dim is too dark / too light | Change the `PF/DialogDim` prefab's Image alpha. There is no other knob, by design. |
| A dialog is undimmed but still blocks input | `PF/DialogDim` failed to load (warned, best-effort). The gate is a separate asset and is unaffected. Check the Addressables entry. |
